D012-D018_h001.question: "It's been a few months now, ever since that accident. I was on a delivery, and there was this really bad pile-up. Saw a lot of blood at the scene... people were really hurt. Now, if I even catch a glimpse of blood, even on TV, I get this intense rush. My heart starts pounding like crazy, I can't catch my breath, and I start sweating and shaking. It's not just the blood, though. I keep reliving it, that crunch of metal, the screams. Sometimes I bolt awake in the middle of the night, covered in sweat, feeling like I'm right back there. I can't seem to get it out of my head, and I've been avoiding that part of town completely."
D012-D018_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h002.question: It's been a few months now, ever since that call... the collapse at the old warehouse. I've been a firefighter for over ten years, been through a lot, but this is different. I can’t shake it. My wife, she’s worried sick about the changes in me. Now, whenever we’re even near a tight spot, like a narrow alley or a building under construction, especially after dark, I just freeze. My heart races, I start sweating, and I feel like I can’t breathe. It’s not just being uncomfortable, it's an immediate, overwhelming panic, like I'm right back in that rubble. Before this, I was fine with enclosed spaces – it was part of the job. But after seeing my buddy get trapped, watching him... I just can’t do it anymore. It’s like the fear of being in tight spaces has completely taken over since that night.
D012-D018_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h003.question: "It’s gotten to the point where I just dread going to campus. Every time I hear a sudden, loud sound – a car horn, a door slamming, even just a book dropping in the hallway – my heart leaps into my throat. I just freeze up, like I can’t move, can’t think, can’t breathe. It reminds me of the earthquake five months ago, when that beam collapsed right next to me in the lab. I had to pull myself out from under the debris. Since then, I can't shake the images and the feeling of being trapped. My wife says I'm withdrawn and jumpy. I keep replaying bits of that day in my head, and I’m having nightmares. It's really affecting my teaching and my research. I just want to feel normal again."
D012-D018_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h004.question: "It's been a while since the bridge collapse – going on seven months now. Everything feels... off. I used to love my job, building things, but now, the thought of even driving over an overpass or going through a tunnel makes my heart race. It's not just a little anxiety; it's an immediate, engulfing terror, like the world is collapsing around me all over again. I start sweating, can't breathe, my hands shake uncontrollably. It's the same feeling I had that day, that helplessness. I keep replaying it, seeing the dust, hearing the screams. Even when I'm home, safe with my wife, I can't shake it. It's like I'm constantly on edge, waiting for something else to go wrong, and it’s made my life a living hell."
D012-D018_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h005.question: Since the accident, things have been so difficult. I'm a pet groomer, and I used to love my job, but now even the thought of a small cut on an animal can send me spiraling. Last week, a dog nicked its paw, and when I saw just a drop of blood, I felt completely frozen, like I couldn't move or breathe. It's like I'm back in that moment, seeing the blood, feeling stuck, unable to do anything. Even looking at a needle on TV makes me feel the same way. It's been happening for months now, ever since that car crash where I was trapped. I'm having terrible nightmares about it, and I can't stop replaying everything in my head. I know it's not just a simple fear anymore; it’s taken over my life since the trauma.
D012-D018_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h006.question: "It’s getting harder to even show up for work, doc. Every time I see blood, or even just think about a bad injury, my heart just pounds out of my chest, I can’t catch my breath, and I start shaking uncontrollably. I have to push through it though, because it's literally my job. But it brings me right back to that accident a few months ago – the one where I saw... well, the one that really messed me up. Since then, it’s not just the blood, it’s like…other things constantly remind me of it, and I can't stop replaying it in my head. I'm always on edge, always looking over my shoulder, and I can't sleep properly. It's been like this for over a month now, and it’s completely draining me."
D012-D018_h006.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D012-D018_h007.question: "It all started after that kitchen accident, doctor. Seeing my own blood, even a tiny cut, just... it sends me into a complete tailspin. I get this cold dread, my heart pounds out of my chest, and I can't breathe. It happened immediately, right after it, and now I can’t even look at a knife without picturing it. I've completely stopped prepping ingredients myself; I make my sous chef do all the cutting. I’ve even cancelled my regular dentist appointments because the thought of a needle… I just can’t. My ex-wife used to say I was being dramatic, but she doesn't understand. She wasn't there when I almost bled out on the kitchen floor. It's not just the blood itself, it brings back everything from that day. I just can't shake it."
D012-D018_h007.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D012-D018_h008.question: I guess it started a few months ago after that awful car crash. I was hit by a truck carrying livestock, and the image of those terrified animals has been burned into my mind. Now, even seeing a dog on the street makes my heart race. I find myself planning my routes to work specifically to avoid parks or areas where I might encounter one. I know it sounds irrational, but the thought of being near any animal, even a small cat, just fills me with dread. It’s gotten so bad that I refused a promotion that would have required me to walk through a different part of the city, all because there’s a small dog park nearby. My friends don’t understand, they say I’m overreacting, but it’s more than just a fear of dogs; it’s like the whole incident is replaying in my head whenever I see them.
D012-D018_h008.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D012-D018_h009.question: I'm here today because things just haven't been right since the accident a few months ago. It was a dog attack, you see – a large, aggressive stray. I was just walking home after a late night restoring a painting, and it came out of nowhere. Ever since then, it's like a switch flipped. I used to love dogs, but now, the thought of them… it sends shivers down my spine. I get this cold, clammy feeling just picturing one. My husband, bless his heart, tries to encourage me to go on walks, but I just can't face it. If I even hear a bark, my heart starts racing and I get so nauseous. Last week, I had to walk past a house with a dog behind a fence, and I was so terrified I nearly had a panic attack, even though I knew it couldn't get to me. I just… I can't shake it. It's like the attack is still happening, over and over, in my head, and now every dog feels like that dog.
D012-D018_h009.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D012-D018_h010.question: "Lately, I just haven't been myself. It all started after that earthquake last year, the big one, you know? Now, every time the sky gets dark or the wind picks up, my heart just starts pounding out of my chest. I get so dizzy, like I can't breathe, and my hands get all clammy. I used to love hiking, but now the thought of being up high, or even seeing a towering building, makes me completely freeze up. I've stopped taking the stairs in my apartment, even if it's just a few flights, and I avoid all the parks with hills. It’s affecting my studies too; I can’t focus, and I keep reliving the feeling of the ground shaking. I just can’t seem to get that day out of my head."
D012-D018_h010.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D012-D018_h011.question: It’s been, what, six months now since the accident? I can barely sleep. Every time I close my eyes, I’m back in that crosswalk, seeing that dog… it came out of nowhere, running full speed, all teeth and snarls. I still feel the impact, the pain. Now, if I even *see* a dog, my heart races, my palms sweat, and I freeze. I have to avoid parks, certain streets, anything with even a whiff of a dog. I can only manage if my daughter is with me, holding my arm, practically steering me away. I know it sounds ridiculous for a man my age, a lawyer even, but it’s real. This isn't just about the dogs; it's what they represent, what they bring back. The nightmares are constant, playing the whole thing over again and again, and I can't shake the feeling of being in danger, even when I know I'm safe at home.
D012-D018_h011.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D012-D018_h012.question: "It's like I'm constantly on edge, doctor. Even a sudden gust of wind or the distant rumble of thunder sends a jolt of terror through me. I know it sounds irrational for a 35-year-old, especially someone pursuing a PhD, but the thought of a storm brewing… it just brings everything back. There was this hurricane a few years ago, when I was doing fieldwork – it was absolutely horrific. I was caught out in it, and honestly, I thought I was going to die. Now, whenever the weather even hints at something similar, my heart pounds, I get dizzy, and I can't focus on my thesis for days. I try to rationalize it, tell myself it’s just rain, but the raw panic is still there. I can't avoid checking the weather forecast compulsively, and if it looks bad, I just brace myself for days of intense anxiety. It's not just a general fear; it’s specifically tied to these violent weather events, and it's been like this ever since that experience. It affects everything."
D012-D018_h012.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D012-D018_h013.question: "It’s been pretty rough since the accident, Doc. I was training a client, demonstrating a lift, and the weight slipped. It crushed my hand. The sight of all that blood… it was just overwhelming. Now, if I even get a small cut, or see an ad for a hospital, I just freeze up. I was even supposed to get a routine flu shot a few weeks ago, but I just couldn't do it. My buddy had to literally drag me out of the clinic. The thought of a needle going in... I start sweating, my heart races. It’s been happening for about eight months now. I keep replaying the incident in my head, the sound of the crash, the feeling of the impact. I can't sleep, and I’m constantly on edge, always looking over my shoulder. It’s hard to focus on my clients; I just feel numb most of the time."
D012-D018_h013.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D012-D018_h014.question:
It's been six months since... the incident. I used to love my job, the rumble of the train, the city lights flashing by. Now, every single time I go into the tunnel, I feel this intense dread. My heart starts pounding, my palms get sweaty, and I feel like I can't breathe. It's not just the tunnel itself, but the memories of that day… the screech of the metal, the screams. I keep replaying it over and over in my head.

I try to tell myself it’s going to be okay, gripping the controls so hard my knuckles turn white. I can barely get through a shift these days. I even asked my supervisor if I could just drive above ground, but that’s not really an option. I know it’s just a tunnel, and I tell myself I’m being irrational, but the fear is so overwhelming. I can almost taste the dust and smell the smoke again. It's like I'm right back there.
D012-D018_h014.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D012-D018_h015.question: It’s all been a bit much, especially since… since the accident last year. I’ve always been a bit cautious, but now, it’s completely taken over. I’m a speech therapist, and my job involves home visits, sometimes in apartment buildings. But the thought of getting into an elevator – it just sends shivers down my spine. I tense up, my heart races… I feel like I can’t breathe. My husband, he usually has to come with me to appointments if there’s no other way to get to a higher floor. I can only manage if he's right there, almost shielding me. It’s not just the elevator itself; it brings back that whole feeling of being trapped and utterly helpless, just like in the car that day. I keep reliving parts of it, especially at night, and I’m always on edge, jumpy at the slightest noise.
D012-D018_h015.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D012-D018_h016.question: "Lately, I just haven't been myself, especially when I'm in the booth. It’s hard to even describe, but every time I see a big truck heading my way, or even just hear that rumbling noise, my heart starts pounding and I can barely breathe. It takes me right back to that pile-up two months ago, where I saw that huge tanker jackknife right in front of my booth. I can still see it in my head clear as day. Now, even just thinking about traffic or a busy day at work makes my stomach churn with dread days before my shift. I know it’s just a toll booth, and it's silly to be this scared, but I literally have to force myself to get in there every morning, feeling absolutely terrified the whole time. It's like I'm stuck in that moment over and over again, and I can't escape it."
D012-D018_h016.options:
A. Binge-Eating Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h017.question: “Thanks for seeing me, Doc. It's gotten to the point where I can barely function. It all started after that accident at the plant six months ago – a conveyor belt malfunctioned right next to me, just a hair’s breadth from serious injury. Ever since then, any loud, sudden noise, especially clanking or grinding, sends me into a full-blown panic. My heart starts hammering, I get short of breath, and I’ll be drenched in sweat. I’ve started actively avoiding the factory floor unless I absolutely have to be there, and even then, I'm on edge, my eyes constantly scanning for hazards. I just can't shake the feeling that it's going to happen again. I keep replaying the incident in my head, seeing the belt coming at me over and over. I don’t sleep well, always waking up in a sweat, and I’m constantly irritable with my wife and the crew. It’s not just the noise; it's everything from that day that haunts me.”
D012-D018_h017.options:
A. Binge-Eating Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h018.question: "I know it sounds silly for a 55-year-old woman, especially one who manages high-stakes property deals, but I can't shake this feeling. It all started after Mark's accident, you know, when I saw… everything. Now, if I even catch a glimpse of blood, even on TV, I freeze. My heart races, I feel utterly paralyzed, like I can't move a muscle. It's not just the sight either; the thought of needles, or any medical procedure really, sends me into a spiral. I’ve had to force myself to get my annual physical, clenching my fists and enduring the whole thing, just to get it over with, even though I'm terrified the entire time. It's been nearly a year and a half, and it’s always present, not just when I see something. It's the constant flashbacks, the nightmares, the way I jump at every unexpected sound. It’s not just the blood, it’s everything that came after it."
D012-D018_h018.options:
A. Binge-Eating Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h019.question: It's been about eight months since the whole ordeal with my neighbor's pitbull, and I just can't shake it. I used to love dogs, you know, as a ghostwriter, I’d often work in coffee shops where people brought their well-behaved pups. But ever since that attack where it came out of nowhere and bit me, just thinking about dogs sends me spiraling. My heart starts pounding like crazy, I can't breathe, and I break out in a cold sweat. It's so bad that if I *have* to be anywhere near one, say, walking down the street and someone's got a dog on a leash, I absolutely have to grab onto my ex-husband or my friend’s arm, whoever I’m with. I just can't face it alone. I relive that moment constantly, and I can hardly sleep.
D012-D018_h019.options:
A. Binge-Eating Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h020.question: "It’s gotten so bad, doctor, I don’t even recognize myself anymore. Since the fire at my old studio, the one where I tragically lost all my designs and my assistant almost didn't make it out, I just can't stand loud noises. It’s been… it’s been about eight months now. The clang of a dropped pot, a car backfiring, even the sound of a balloon popping – it sends me into an absolute frenzy. I feel this suffocating terror immediately, like the floor is going to drop out from under me. I try to avoid any place where it might be noisy. I can barely even stay at my new studio unless my best friend is right there with me, or I'm clutching my grandmother's old thimble. It's the only way I can even begin to cope. I know it sounds ridiculous for a 31-year-old, but I just can't shake this feeling of constant dread and being on edge."
D012-D018_h020.options:
A. Binge-Eating Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h021.question: "I know it might sound a bit silly for someone who helps people find love, but I can barely leave my house these days. It started after that terrible car accident a few months ago – the one where I was stuck in the flipped car for what felt like an eternity. Now, any time I have to get in a car, especially if it's an enclosed space like a tunnel or even just heavy traffic, I get this overwhelming sense of dread. My heart pounds, I sweat, I feel like I can't breathe... it's pure panic. I force myself to do it for work, to meet clients, but I'm just enduring it, white-knuckling the whole drive, replaying bits of the crash in my head, the feeling of being trapped. Before the accident, I was fine with driving; now, the thought of being in an enclosed space with no escape just brings it all back."
D012-D018_h021.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D018_h022.question:
Lately, I’ve been feeling on edge, jumpy, like I did for months after the tornado. That whole incident was just… terrifying. I still see flashes of the overturned kennels and hear the shrieking animals in my head, especially when the weather turns. It’s been almost a year since it happened, and every time the sky darkens, my heart starts pounding and I can barely breathe.

I know it’s just a storm, and I hate that I can’t control this feeling, but it’s like I’m right back there. My ex-husband said I was being dramatic even before the divorce. Work is a nightmare too; even during routine weather checks, I find myself bracing, my hands shaking. I try to push through, telling myself it’s silly, but the anxiety is suffocating. I can't shake the feeling of impending doom, and it's exhausting.
D012-D018_h022.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D018_h023.question: It all started after that accident on the site, about six months ago. A beam slipped and nearly crushed me, and I saw… a lot of blood. Ever since, I can’t stand the sight of it. Even a small cut sends me into a panic. I had to get a tetanus shot a few weeks back, and I almost passed out. My buddy had to hold my hand the whole time, and I kept my eyes squeezed shut. It’s not just the blood, though. I can’t stop thinking about what happened. I’m constantly on edge, jumping at every loud noise, and I can’t sleep right. When I do, I’m back there, seeing it all over again. I barely leave the house anymore, and when I do, I’m hyper-aware of everything around me, always expecting something bad to happen again. It's like the world just isn't safe anymore.
D012-D018_h023.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D018_h024.question: It's been a few months now, ever since that accident at the plant. I was welding a pipe, just like any other day, and then the unthinkable happened. A piece of shrapnel flew off, hit a line, and a co-worker... well, he was pretty badly cut. There was so much blood. More than I've ever seen. I know it’s crazy, but now, the sight of even a little cut gives me the jitters. I can barely handle being in a doctor's office, especially if they're talking about needles or drawing blood. I get this overwhelming sense of panic, like I'm right back there. My wife has to come with me to any appointments, I just can't face it alone. I feel like I'm constantly on edge, always looking over my shoulder since then. I haven't been sleeping well either; every time I close my eyes, I see it all again.
D012-D018_h024.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D018_h025.question: "It's like the world just turned upside down that night, the rain, the wind... I still get a knot in my stomach just thinking about it. Ever since the hurricane, I just can't deal with bad weather. I used to love a good storm, but now... the sight of dark clouds, the sound of thunder... it sends me into a complete panic. I've even changed my work shifts so I don't have to drive in the dark during the rainy season. I'll take a longer route to avoid an area that flooded, even if it means being late. It's not just the weather, though. I keep replaying bits of that night over and over, waking up in cold sweats, and my temper's been on a hair-trigger. It’s been going on for months now, well over half a year. I used to be so organized at work, but now I can barely focus. I just want to stop feeling this constant dread."
D012-D018_h025.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
